## Two figures  
China, Qing dynasty (1644- 1911), 18th or early 19th century Kezi (silk tapestry), panel, 60.1 x 39.5 cm Gift of Dr Lam Kwok Pun HKUT2008.1664  
The two figures wear the distinctive clothing of scholar officials. While sightseeing on a mountain, they are surrounded by bats and clouds, which symbolic wealth and good fortune. Distinctive sawtooth patterns appear between the area of color due to the unique processes involved in making silk. Weavers use a shuttle to carry polychrome weft threads across the warp- not the entire textile- leaving a subtle space between the colours. Known as tangling daimons (continuous warp and broken weft), this technique gives its unique appearance, as it is thought to resemble cut or carved silk. The shading of the green and blue slopes was achieved by using the chandgusaing (long and short propping) technique. The offsetting rows of threads often create the striking edge zags patterns that are seen here on the edge of the colour blocks.
